title: Large Language Models for Education and Research: An Empirical and User Survey-based Analysis
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how two large language models, ChatGPT and DeepSeek, compare in education and research contexts. The authors argue that although both tools are increasingly used for tasks such as tutoring, lecture preparation, coding support, research assistance, and problem solving, prior work has not systematically compared them on both technical performance and user perceptions. The study therefore asks how the models differ in accuracy, efficiency, programming performance, and practical usefulness for academic and research activities.

The study combines three components: a background technology analysis of the two models, empirical task-based benchmarking, and a user survey. In the empirical component, ChatGPT and DeepSeek were tested on mathematics, language tasks, scientific problem solving, medical applications, and Codeforces programming problems. Their outputs were compared using task outcomes and text/code similarity metrics such as ROUGE, BLEU, and BERTScore, with some responses validated by subject-matter experts. The user survey gathered both rating-scale and open-ended responses about model effectiveness, reliability, usefulness for writing, coding, lecture preparation, literature summarization, and idea generation.

The participant context for the survey included a mix of undergraduates, postgraduates, doctoral students, academic staff, and independent researchers. Most respondents came from computer science and engineering-related disciplines, with smaller representation from AI, science, health, business, medicine, and agriculture. This places the study primarily in higher education and academic/professional research settings rather than in K-12 schooling. The paper does not describe a classroom intervention; instead, it examines existing use and perceptions of AI tools alongside experimental benchmarking tasks.

The main conclusions are that ChatGPT is generally perceived as stronger in fluency, creativity, educational relevance, writing support, summarization, and idea generation, while DeepSeek performs especially well in programming and structured reasoning tasks. In the experiments, both models handled math, language, science, and medical tasks well, but DeepSeek achieved stronger performance on the programming benchmark. Survey responses also highlighted limitations, including hallucinated or incorrect answers, weak referencing, calculation mistakes, slow responses, and concerns about overreliance on AI. Overall, the authors conclude that both systems have strong potential to support education and research, with complementary strengths that could be used responsibly in academic settings.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-family conversational large language model used for text generation, explanation, coding assistance, and academic support tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Compared with DeepSeek in empirical tasks relevant to education and research, including mathematics problem solving, language tasks, scientific problem solving, medical diagnostic/reporting tasks, programming problems, and user-perceived usefulness for educational and research activities.

findings.finding_summary: In mathematics, ChatGPT produced mathematically valid and complete step-by-step solutions to a classical Fourier series expansion problem, as reviewed by subject-matter experts. In language tasks, it also performed consistently well in grammar correction, paraphrasing, and abstractive summarization, evaluated against human-written references using ROUGE and BLEU, though no aggregate scores were reported.
findings.measure: Expert review of Fourier series solution validity; ROUGE and BLEU for grammar correction, paraphrasing, and abstractive summarization

findings.finding_summary: On structured physics, chemistry, and biology problem sets, ChatGPT was reported to perform well; a chemistry expert validated 100% correctness on the tested chemistry problems. The paper states this demonstrates utility in domain-specific reasoning when prompts are clear.
findings.measure: Expert-validated correctness on structured science problem sets

findings.finding_summary: For medical diagnostic and reporting tasks, ChatGPT achieved approximately 90% accuracy when benchmarked against gold-standard clinical references. The paper presents this as evidence of strong medically accurate output, though task counts are not given.
findings.measure: Accuracy against gold-standard clinical references on diagnostic/reporting tasks

findings.finding_summary: On a curated set of seven Codeforces problems (difficulty 800 to 2200), ChatGPT solved most problems but had failures due to wrong answers, time limit exceeded, and compile errors. Success counts were 5/5 on Problems A, B, F, and G; 4/5 on Problems C and D; and 3/5 on Problem E, with BLEU scores ranging from 0.10 to 0.34 and BERTScore from 0.71 to 0.77 versus human solutions.
findings.measure: Programming problem success/failure on Codeforces; BLEU and BERTScore similarity to human solutions
findings.effect_size: Problem A: 5/5, BLEU 0.34, BERT 0.77; Problem B: 5/5, BLEU 0.18, BERT 0.71; Problem C: 4/5, BLEU 0.12, BERT 0.71; Problem D: 4/5, BLEU 0.27, BERT 0.77; Problem E: 3/5, BLEU 0.10, BERT 0.72; Problem F: 5/5, BLEU 0.23, BERT 0.77; Problem G: 5/5, BLEU 0.14, BERT 0.72
findings.sample_size: n=35 generated solutions (7 problems x 5 attempts)

findings.finding_summary: In the user survey, ChatGPT was generally rated more favorably than DeepSeek on response accuracy, relevance to education, helpfulness in research, lecture preparation, and creative response. The modal ratings were 4 for ChatGPT in each of these categories, with participant shares of 45.8%, 58.3%, 41.7%, 36.4%, and 41.7%, respectively.
findings.measure: User ratings (1-5 scale) across educational/research support dimensions
findings.effect_size: Response Accuracy: rating 4 by 45.8%; Relevance to Education: rating 4 by 58.3%; Helpful in Research: rating 4 by 41.7%; Lecture Preparation: rating 4 by 36.4%; Creative Response: rating 4 by 41.7%

findings.finding_summary: Survey respondents preferred ChatGPT for multiple academic tasks: writing/proofreading assignments (17 preferred ChatGPT, 3 DeepSeek, 4 both), coding help/debugging (12 ChatGPT, 3 DeepSeek, 9 both), preparing lectures and teaching slides (13 ChatGPT, 2 DeepSeek, 8 both, 1 neither), literature summarization (18 ChatGPT, 1 DeepSeek, 5 both), and generating research ideas (14 ChatGPT, 0 DeepSeek, 9 both, 1 neither). Additionally, 58.3% identified ChatGPT as the most reliable tool for education and research.
findings.measure: Task preference counts and perceived reliability in survey
findings.effect_size: Writing/proofreading: 17 ChatGPT vs 3 DeepSeek vs 4 both; Coding/debugging: 12 vs 3 vs 9 both; Lectures/slides: 13 vs 2 vs 8 both vs 1 neither; Literature summarization: 18 vs 1 vs 5 both; Research ideas: 14 vs 0 vs 9 both vs 1 neither; Reliability: 58.3% ChatGPT
findings.sample_size: n=24 inferred from survey percentages and task counts

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek is a family of reasoning- and efficiency-focused large language models used for structured question answering, coding, mathematical reasoning, and technical assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Compared with ChatGPT in empirical tasks relevant to education and research, including mathematics problem solving, language tasks, scientific problem solving, medical diagnostic/reporting tasks, programming problems, and user-perceived usefulness for educational and research activities.

findings.finding_summary: In mathematics, DeepSeek produced mathematically valid and complete step-by-step solutions to a classical Fourier series expansion problem, as reviewed by subject-matter experts. In language tasks, it also performed consistently well in grammar correction, paraphrasing, and abstractive summarization, evaluated against human-written references using ROUGE and BLEU, though no aggregate scores were reported.
findings.measure: Expert review of Fourier series solution validity; ROUGE and BLEU for grammar correction, paraphrasing, and abstractive summarization

findings.finding_summary: On structured physics, chemistry, and biology problem sets, DeepSeek was reported to perform well; a chemistry expert validated 100% correctness on the tested chemistry problems. The paper states this demonstrates utility in domain-specific reasoning when prompts are clear.
findings.measure: Expert-validated correctness on structured science problem sets

findings.finding_summary: For medical diagnostic and reporting tasks, DeepSeek achieved approximately 90% accuracy when benchmarked against gold-standard clinical references. The paper presents this as evidence of strong medically accurate output, though task counts are not given.
findings.measure: Accuracy against gold-standard clinical references on diagnostic/reporting tasks

findings.finding_summary: On the curated set of seven Codeforces problems (difficulty 800 to 2200), DeepSeek achieved a perfect success rate across all evaluated problems. Its solutions also aligned more closely with human baselines than ChatGPT's, with BLEU scores from 0.16 to 0.51 and BERTScore from 0.73 to 0.84; the paper also states DeepSeek achieved the highest ROUGE-L of 0.55 on the 800-rated task.
findings.measure: Programming problem success/failure on Codeforces; BLEU, BERTScore, and reported ROUGE-L similarity to human solutions
findings.effect_size: Problem A: 5/5, BLEU 0.51, BERT 0.84, ROUGE-L 0.55; Problem B: 5/5, BLEU 0.33, BERT 0.79; Problem C: 5/5, BLEU 0.16, BERT 0.78; Problem D: 5/5, BLEU 0.25, BERT 0.81; Problem E: 5/5, BLEU 0.23, BERT 0.73; Problem F: 5/5, BLEU 0.33, BERT 0.81; Problem G: 5/5, BLEU 0.18, BERT 0.73
findings.sample_size: n=35 generated solutions (7 problems x 5 attempts)

findings.finding_summary: In the user survey, DeepSeek was generally rated below ChatGPT on response accuracy, relevance to education, helpfulness in research, lecture preparation, and creative response, with modal ratings of 3 in most of these categories. However, it was rated comparatively better for coding, where 50.0% of participants assigned it a rating of 4.
findings.measure: User ratings (1-5 scale) across educational/research support dimensions
findings.effect_size: Response Accuracy: rating 3 by 45.8%; Relevance to Education: rating 4 by 37.5%; Helpful in Research: rating 3 by 33.3%; Lecture Preparation: rating 3 by 45.5%; Creative Response: rating 3 by 45.8%; Coding: rating 4 by 50.0%

findings.finding_summary: Survey task preferences showed limited preference for DeepSeek alone on most academic tasks, but some relative strength in coding support and lecture preparation. Counts were writing/proofreading (3 preferred DeepSeek), coding help/debugging (3), preparing lectures/slides (2), literature summarization (1), and generating research ideas (0); 4.2% of respondents considered DeepSeek the most reliable tool, while 29.2% said reliability is task-dependent and 8.3% rated both tools equally.
findings.measure: Task preference counts and perceived reliability in survey
findings.effect_size: Writing/proofreading: 3 DeepSeek; Coding/debugging: 3; Lectures/slides: 2; Literature summarization: 1; Research ideas: 0; Reliability: 4.2% DeepSeek most reliable
findings.sample_size: n=24 inferred from survey percentages and task counts

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical comparative study with benchmarks and a user survey, but it does not report a randomized or quasi-experimental educational design, and key methodological details such as task sample sizes for several domains and survey sampling procedures are limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports generally positive performance and user perceptions, especially strong coding results for DeepSeek, but no standardized causal effect sizes on student learning outcomes are provided, so educational impact remains promising but unclear.
